title: Rothschild Investment Corp IL Decreases Holdings in Apple (AAPL)

text:
Posted by Jennifer Salazar on May 4th, 2018 // No Comments
Rothschild Investment Corp IL cut its stake in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 2.5% in the fourth quarter, according to its most recent Form 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The firm owned 196,032 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 4,965 shares during the quarter. Apple makes up approximately 3.6% of Rothschild Investment Corp IL’s investment portfolio, making the stock its largest position. Rothschild Investment Corp IL’s holdings in Apple were worth $33,175,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period.
Other large investors also recently made changes to their positions in the company. Hennessy Advisors Inc. grew its holdings in Apple by 84.0% in the 4th quarter. Hennessy Advisors Inc. now owns 28,249 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $4,781,000 after buying an additional 12,899 shares in the last quarter. Livingston Group Asset Management CO operating as Southport Capital Management grew its holdings in Apple by 13.3% in the 4th quarter. Livingston Group Asset Management CO operating as Southport Capital Management now owns 56,115 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $9,498,000 after buying an additional 6,570 shares in the last quarter. James Investment Research Inc. grew its holdings in Apple by 7.7% in the 4th quarter. James Investment Research Inc. now owns 87,725 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $14,846,000 after buying an additional 6,248 shares in the last quarter. California Capital Advisors Inc. grew its holdings in Apple by 11.8% in the 4th quarter. California Capital Advisors Inc. now owns 38,111 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $6,449,000 after buying an additional 4,031 shares in the last quarter. Finally, Regentatlantic Capital LLC grew its holdings in Apple by 4.4% in the 4th quarter. Regentatlantic Capital LLC now owns 216,675 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $36,668,000 after buying an additional 9,112 shares in the last quarter. 61.18% of the stock is owned by institutional investors. Several brokerages have recently commented on AAPL. DZ Bank reaffirmed a “buy” rating on shares of Apple in a research note on Thursday. Zacks Investment Research raised Apple from a “sell” rating to a “hold” rating in a research note on Thursday. ValuEngine raised Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a research note on Wednesday. Morningstar set a $175.00 target price on Apple and gave the stock a “neutral” rating in a research note on Wednesday. Finally, Atlantic Securities reissued a “neutral” rating and set a $185.00 target price on shares of Apple in a research note on Wednesday. One analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have given a hold rating, thirty-three have given a buy rating and two have issued a strong buy rating to the company. The stock has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $204.00.
NASDAQ:AAPL opened at $176.89 on Friday. Apple has a 52 week low of $142.20 and a 52 week high of $183.50. The company has a market cap of $858,015.69, a PE ratio of 19.21, a P/E/G ratio of 1.29 and a beta of 1.26. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74, a current ratio of 1.24 and a quick ratio of 1.20.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last issued its quarterly earnings data on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, topping analysts’ consensus estimates of $2.69 by $0.04. Apple had a return on equity of 39.33% and a net margin of 21.55%. The business had revenue of $61.14 billion during the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $60.94 billion. During the same period in the prior year, the company posted $2.10 EPS. The business’s revenue for the quarter was up 15.6% compared to the same quarter last year. equities research analysts anticipate that Apple will post 11.28 EPS for the current year.
The firm also recently disclosed a quarterly dividend, which will be paid on Thursday, May 17th. Investors of record on Monday, May 14th will be issued a $0.73 dividend. This represents a $2.92 dividend on an annualized basis and a yield of 1.65%. This is a positive change from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. The ex-dividend date is Friday, May 11th. Apple’s dividend payout ratio is 27.36%.
Apple announced that its board has authorized a share repurchase program on Tuesday, May 1st that permits the company to repurchase $100.00 billion in shares. This repurchase authorization permits the iPhone maker to purchase up to 11.9% of its stock through open market purchases. Stock repurchase programs are typically a sign that the company’s board of directors believes its stock is undervalued.
In other Apple news, insider Philip W. Schiller sold 69,491 shares of the company’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Tuesday, April 3rd. The stock was sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total value of $11,564,692.22. The transaction was disclosed in a filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which can be accessed through the SEC website . Also, insider Luca Maestri sold 39,122 shares of the company’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Friday, April 13th. The stock was sold at an average price of $174.66, for a total value of $6,833,048.52. Following the completion of the sale, the insider now owns 64,475 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $11,261,203.50. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Insiders sold a total of 125,988 shares of company stock valued at $21,336,201 over the last three months. Corporate insiders own 0.08% of the company’s stock.
